top_story: As winter closes in on Gaza, the 2 November contraction in UN food support and the continued restriction of aid have deepened hunger and left families trying to reinforce damaged shelters with few resources. By 5 November, children were returning to classrooms for the first formal school year since the war’s devastation even as Israeli fire and airstrikes were hitting pupils, teachers, and university sites, turning education into another front of civilian exposure. The same day, additional tanker damage in the Strait of Hormuz showed Iran sustaining pressure in Gulf shipping lanes after the US vote, extending regional instability from maritime trade to already shattered civilian life. The emerging picture is of a region where coercive pressure is falling hardest on civilians, with Gaza’s social recovery and basic survival under immediate strain.
